explain.say: A blast furnace is a tall steel tower lined with heat-proof brick. Iron ore, rock rich in iron oxide, goes in at the top in layers with coke, a form of carbon made from coal, and limestone.

explain.say: Limestone joins with the sand and rock in the ore to make a liquid called slag, which floats on the heavier molten iron. Both are tapped off at the bottom, and the furnace runs nonstop for years.

faq.q: What goes into a blast furnace?
faq.a: Three things go in at the top: iron ore, which is iron oxide in rock; coke, nearly pure carbon made by baking coal; and limestone. Hot air is blown in near the bottom.
asks: What are the raw materials for making iron?

faq.q: How does carbon monoxide turn ore into iron?
faq.a: Carbon monoxide takes oxygen away from iron oxide, becoming carbon dioxide and leaving iron metal behind. Removing oxygen from a substance is called reduction.
asks: What is the chemical reaction in a blast furnace?

faq.q: Why is hot air blown into a blast furnace?
faq.a: The hot blast, preheated to over 1,000 degrees Celsius, makes the coke burn much hotter and faster. This provides the heat to melt the iron and makes the carbon monoxide that reduces the ore.
asks: Why is it called a blast furnace?

faq.a: Slag is the molten waste formed when limestone reacts with sand and other rock in the ore. It is lighter than iron, so it floats on top and is drained off separately. Cooled slag is used to make cement and roads.
asks: What is limestone for in a blast furnace?

faq.q: What happens to the iron from a blast furnace?
faq.a: The iron, called pig iron, contains about 4 percent carbon, which makes it hard but brittle. Most is taken still molten to a steelworks, where extra carbon is removed to make steel.

facts: Blast furnace iron, called pig iron, contains about 4 percent carbon, which makes it brittle.
A large blast furnace can run continuously for 15 to 20 years before it needs relining.

quiz.say: Which gas takes the oxygen away from iron ore in a blast furnace?
quiz.why: Carbon monoxide from the burning coke reduces iron oxide to iron, becoming carbon dioxide.

wrong.1: Nitrogen from the air passes through without reacting.
wrong.2: Steam is not the reducing gas; carbon monoxide does the work.

quiz.say: Why does slag come out above the iron?

options.show: It is less dense than molten iron
options.say: It is less dense than molten iron

options.show: It is hotter than the iron
options.say: It is hotter than the iron

quiz.why: Slag is lighter than iron, so it floats on top and can be drained off separately.

wrong.1: Both are at a similar temperature; density decides which floats.
wrong.2: Slag forms inside the furnace from limestone and rock, not added at the end.
